title: Connected homogeneous int8 with resident and direct-bundle workers

training_method.label: Frozen-base QKV LoRA
training_method.description: Rank-4 QKV adapters return complete summed FP32 gradients to canonical coordinator AdamW.

execution_topology.label: Authenticated mixed-placement campaign
execution_topology.description: One resident-converted and one direct-bundle worker contribute disjoint shards for two steps, with coordinator restart between steps.

memory_profiles.label: Authenticated resident conversion
memory_profiles.description: Fetch and authenticate the complete FP32 base, load it, then replace every frozen linear with owned int8 buffers.

memory_profiles.label: Authenticated direct bundle int8
memory_profiles.description: Authenticate and quantize one frozen-linear shard at a time without complete FP32 linear residency.

numerical_profiles.label: Per-output symmetric int8 with FP32 dequantization
numerical_profiles.description: Frozen linears retain int8 weights plus FP32 scales/biases; forward/backward reconstruct FP32 while LoRA and submitted gradients remain FP32.

numerical_profiles.label: Exact CPU FP32 reference
numerical_profiles.description: Separate bit-exact worker-acceptance profile used only to measure trajectory separation.

worker_profiles.label: Resident-converted native int8
worker_profiles.description: Persistent Python/PyTorch CPU worker with complete authenticated-base conversion.

worker_profiles.label: Direct-bundle native int8
worker_profiles.description: Persistent Python/PyTorch CPU worker constructing from individually authenticated bundle shards.

reproduction.notes: The proof uses two local authenticated native sessions over loopback, restarts the coordinator after step 1, writes no credential to the committed result, and compares the final int8 adapter with a separately trained exact-FP32 reference.
